html:
A policy under which millions of young city people in China were sent to live and work in the countryside, mostly between 1968 and 1980. About 17 million went.

It began in the 1950s on a small scale, but Mao Zedong made it a mass campaign in December 1968, during the Cultural Revolution. Sending the "educated youth" to learn from peasants also broke up the Red Guards, whose factions had fought each other in the cities, and it eased a lack of urban jobs.

Many of the sent-down youth spent years in remote villages and state farms, from Heilongjiang to Yunnan, with little schooling. Some later called themselves a lost generation. After Mao's death most went home, and the campaign ended around 1980, as reform and opening began. Among those sent down was Xi Jinping, who spent seven years in a Shaanxi village.
sum: A policy under which millions of young city people in China were sent to live and work in the countryside, mostly between 1968 and 1980. About 17 million went.
